title: B1 · L14 — Non-defining relative clauses
description: Oraciones relativas explicativas que añaden información extra (no esencial) sobre el sustantivo. Se separan con comas y no admiten 'that'.

questions.prompt: Le hablas a un amigo sobre la visita de tu hermana.
questions.question: Complete: 'My sister, ___ lives in Berlin, is coming to visit us.'
questions.explanation: En relativas NO DEFINIDORAS para personas se usa 'who' — NUNCA 'that'. Las comas aíslan la información extra (que se puede omitir sin perder el sentido). Error típico del hispanohablante: usar 'that' entre comas por analogía con 'que' en español.
examples: My mother, who is a doctor, works incredibly long hours. → info extra sobre mother
Tom, who studied in Paris, speaks French fluently. → dato adicional sobre Tom

questions.prompt: Describes un monumento famoso en un texto turístico.
questions.question: Choose: 'The Eiffel Tower, ___ is in Paris, is a famous landmark.'
questions.explanation: 'Which' → cosas en relativas no definidoras. La info entre comas es EXTRA: aunque la omitamos, sabemos qué es la Torre Eiffel. Error típico: usar 'that' (prohibido en no definidoras) o 'where' (que sería para el lugar mismo, no para dar dato sobre la torre).
examples: The Nile, which is the longest river in the world, flows through Africa. → dato extra
London, which has around 9 million people, is a major city. → info adicional

questions.statement: In non-defining relative clauses, 'that' can be used instead of 'who' or 'which'.
questions.explanation: FALSO. 'That' está PROHIBIDO en relativas no definidoras (las de comas). Solo son válidos: who (personas), which (cosas), whose (posesión), where (lugares), when (tiempos). Este es error TOP en estudiantes que aprenden 'that' como comodín en definidoras.
examples: Correct: My car, which is red, is parked outside. → 'which' en no definidora
Incorrect: My car, that is red, is parked outside. → 'that' NO permitido

questions.text: My best friend, who I have known for years, is getting married.
questions.explanation: Nota las pausas al leer las comas — son cortas pero perceptibles: 'my best friend [pausa] who I've known for years [pausa] is getting married'. En habla natural la contracción 'who I've known' es la norma. 'Who' aquí es OBLIGATORIO (no se puede omitir en no definidoras, incluso siendo objeto).
examples: Emma, who I met at university, is now my colleague. → info extra + pausas
Tom, who I've known since childhood, lives abroad now. → dato biográfico

questions.prompt: Identifica la frase con puntuación correcta de relativa no definidora.
questions.question: Which sentence is correctly punctuated as a non-defining relative clause?
options: The man who called me was my brother.
My brother who lives in Rome is visiting.
My brother, who lives in Rome, is visiting.
My brother that lives in Rome is visiting.
questions.explanation: Solo la opción C tiene las comas correctas. 'My brother' ya identifica a la persona única (tengo un solo hermano), así que la relativa es EXTRA. Sin comas (B) sugiere que tengo varios hermanos y este es el de Roma. Opción D usa 'that' — prohibido en no definidoras.
examples: My father, who is 60, is still very active. → info extra sobre única persona
Barcelona, which is my hometown, is absolutely beautiful. → dato extra sobre ciudad única

questions.prompt: Empareja cada tipo de relativa con sus características:
questions.explanation: Diferencias clave: (1) puntuación (con/sin comas), (2) tipo de información (esencial/extra), (3) uso de 'that' (permitido/prohibido), (4) omisión del pronombre (posible en definidoras si es objeto; nunca en no definidoras). Las comas son la pista visual más clara.
examples: Defining: The man (who) I met yesterday was kind. → 'who' omisible
Non-defining: John, who I met yesterday, was kind. → 'who' obligatorio

questions.prompt: Escribes sobre el clima de la capital española.
questions.question: Complete: 'Madrid, ___ is the capital of Spain, has hot summers.'
questions.explanation: 'Madrid' está identificada por el nombre propio → la información sobre la capital es EXTRA (no definidora). Se usa 'which' con comas. Error típico: usar 'that' (prohibido en no definidoras) o 'who' (que solo va con personas).
examples: Paris, which is famous for its museums, attracts millions of tourists. → dato extra
Tokyo, which is huge, is surprisingly organised. → info adicional

questions.target: My grandmother, who lived to 95, told the most wonderful stories, honestly.
questions.explanation: Situación: hablas de un familiar querido en una conversación personal. No definidora: 'my grandmother' ya está identificada (una sola abuela concreta), la cláusula 'who lived to 95' es dato extra. Pausas al leer las comas. 'Honestly' como cierre emocional natural.
examples: My uncle, who is a chef, cooks the most amazing paella ever. → familiar + dato + opinión
My best friend, who lives abroad, calls me every week without fail. → relación + hábito

questions.statement: The commas around a non-defining relative clause work like brackets — you could remove the clause and the sentence would still make sense.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Las comas funcionan como paréntesis (parenthetical commas): aíslan información NO esencial que se puede eliminar sin que la oración pierda sentido. Test rápido: si al quitar la parte entre comas la frase sigue teniendo sentido completo → es no definidora.
examples: My brother (who lives in Rome) is visiting. → My brother is visiting. → sigue teniendo sentido
London (which is expensive) is exciting. → London is exciting. → info principal completa

questions.prompt: Hablas de un equipo deportivo con conexión personal.
questions.question: Choose: 'The team, ___ captain is my cousin, won the match.'
questions.explanation: 'Whose' expresa POSESIÓN también en relativas no definidoras. 'Whose captain' = 'their captain' → posesión colectiva. Error típico: usar 'which' o 'who' que no marcan posesión, o confundir 'whose' (posesivo) con 'who's' (contracción de 'who is').
examples: The company, whose CEO is famous, is expanding globally. → posesión + info extra
The band, whose singer is my friend, is playing tonight. → conexión personal

questions.text: Barcelona, which is my favourite city in Europe, has beautiful architecture.
questions.explanation: Nota las pausas al leer — corresponden a las comas. 'Which is' se pronuncia con weak form, casi 'wichizmy'. Barcelona ya está identificada por el nombre propio → info entre comas es EXTRA. Estructura clásica: [nombre propio], which + info personal, + verbo principal.
examples: Rome, which is full of history, is absolutely stunning. → ciudad + opinión + valoración
Amsterdam, which is known for its canals, is a must-visit. → ciudad + fama + recomendación

questions.prompt: Identifica la frase con puntuación o pronombre incorrecto.
questions.question: Which is INCORRECT?
options: My phone, which is new, has stopped working.
My phone that is new has stopped working. (extra info)
My sister, who lives in Rome, is visiting.
Paris, where I studied, is beautiful.
questions.explanation: La opción B mezcla estilos: usa 'that' (definidora) pero pretende dar info extra. Si la información es extra, DEBE usar comas y 'which', no 'that'. Las demás opciones (A, C, D) están correctamente puntuadas y usan el pronombre adecuado.
examples: My phone, which is new, has stopped working. → no definidora correcta
The phone that I bought last week is new. → definidora sin comas

questions.statement: In speaking, non-defining clauses are often marked by short pauses where the commas would be.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. En habla, las relativas no definidoras se marcan con PAUSAS breves donde estarían las comas. Además la entonación baja ligeramente en la parte entre pausas. Esta prosodia distingue clara la info principal de la extra en el discurso oral.
examples: My brother [pause] who lives in Rome [pause] is visiting. → pausas orales
Madrid [pause] which is the capital of Spain [pause] is hot in summer. → entonación baja

questions.prompt: Hablas nostálgicamente de la década en que naciste.
questions.question: Choose: 'The 1990s, ___ I was born, was a great decade.'
questions.explanation: 'When' → relativo para TIEMPO/momentos. Aquí va entre comas porque la info es EXTRA (los 90 ya están identificados). Errores: (A) 'which' no encaja para 'in which'; (C) 'where' es lugar; (D) 'who' es persona.
examples: In 2010, when I moved to London, life completely changed for me. → año + momento
Last summer, when it was really hot, we stayed inside all day. → estación + info extra

questions.target: My apartment, which has a lovely balcony, is honestly my favourite place to relax.
questions.explanation: Situación: describes tu casa con detalles personales en una conversación. No definidora con 'which' + comas para info extra. 'Honestly' + valoración emocional 'favourite place to relax' hacen la frase natural. Muy útil para describir posesiones con matices personales.
examples: My car, which is really quite old, still runs perfectly, believe it or not. → objeto + dato + valoración
My hometown, which is fairly small, is honestly so peaceful. → lugar + característica + emoción
